title: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning
hosting_unit: School of Computer and Information Sciences

first_offered.uncertainty: Catalog states Fall 2025 applications for Fall 2026 admittance; actual first enrollment not independently verified.

overview: The 180-credit BS in Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning combines computing, AI, mathematics, sciences and humanities with design projects, a year-long team capstone and either one or three co-op experiences.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning

outcomes.text: Identify problems suited to AI or machine-learning solutions.
Interpret and communicate statistical and algorithmic results.
Collaborate to design and implement AI/ML systems.
Apply mathematical, algorithmic and computing foundations to evaluate system design tradeoffs.
Use software-engineering methods to construct and evaluate AI/ML systems.
Explain the ethical and legal implications of AI/ML results and applications.

notes: Main degree requirements are extracted; sample plans are not treated as authoritative individual course-credit sources. Calendar is explicitly quarter; credit figures are preserved with unknown normalization until the credit-hour definition is verified.
Choose eight elective courses; sequence components count individually only if not used for another degree requirement. At most one of the two High Performance Computing sequences may be selected.

ECEC 455 is printed without a linked title in the ECE 350 / MATH 221 sequence. It remains a requirement note rather than an invented course record. The applicability of this apparently incomplete sequence needs catalog clarification.
Science electives use open 100–400-level BMES/BIO/CHEM/ENVS/GEO/PHEV/PHYS ranges; free electives use unrestricted 099–499 courses. These inventories are not expanded.
The math sequence permits replacing MATH 200 with CS 270, ECE 232, ENGR 232 or unused MATH coursework. Those substitute descriptions/titles and the open MATH range remain unverified.
Three post-first-year writing-intensive courses are required, including two in the major; transfer students require advising review. Current WI attributes are not extracted.
No public course sites or syllabi were verified; prerequisites and missing individual course credits remain null.
